error_message: Vietnamese tone marks dropped when rendering opencode output in the terminal. Base vowels with circumflex (ô ê â) showed, but tone marks were lost: 'bạn'->'ban', 'cụ thể'->'cu thê', 'kiểu'->'kiêu'. User suspected line-height clipping.
root_cause: NOT a line-height issue (panel_line_height 22 vs panel_font_size 14 is generous). The terminal grid stores one Unicode scalar per cell: print_char_at_cursor always wrote the char and advanced the cursor, with no handling for zero-width combining marks. The ANSI parser emits each codepoint as a separate PrintChar with no normalization. So a combining tone mark (e.g. precomposed 'ô' U+00F4 followed by combining dot-below U+0323) landed in its own cell, advancing the cursor; the lone mark shaped in isolation rendered clipped/invisible and the base lost its tone.
fix: Added unicode-normalization dep. In print_char_at_cursor, detect combining marks via unicode_normalization::char::is_combining_mark; instead of consuming a cell, fold the mark into the previous cell's base char by NFC-normalizing base+mark (grapheme.nfc()). NFC reorders marks canonically first, so it composes even when the stream sends marks out of canonical order (pairwise char::compose alone misses 'ô'+U+0323 -> 'ộ' because ộ decomposes to ọ+circumflex). Only adopt the result if it collapses to a single scalar; otherwise keep base and drop mark to avoid misaligning the fixed-width grid. Cursor not advanced (zero-width). Tests: combining_marks_fold_into_base_cell, stacked_combining_marks_compose_incrementally, precomposed_vietnamese_passes_through, leading_combining_mark_is_dropped_not_misaligned.

error_message: External file changes (create/delete/rename + content edits) do not update the IDE: open file, edit it elsewhere, IDE does not refresh at all
root_cause: The notify file-watch worker emitted FileSystemEvents via emit_message (no wake) and dispatch.rs never passed event_proxy into run_file_watch_request. With ControlFlow::Wait the winit loop stayed asleep, so FileSystemEvents sat unconsumed in the mpsc channel until an unrelated event (keypress/mouse/terminal/1s poll tick) woke it. The whole notify path (workspace rescan, file-picker refresh, conflict detection, rename/delete handling) was effectively dead; only the 1s mtime poll over OPEN buffers worked, so tree-level changes never appeared.
fix: Passed event_proxy into run_file_watch_request and switched the FileSystemEvents emit to emit_message_and_wake (#1). Also: auto-restart watcher with backoff on failure (#4); non-recursive watch for files opened outside workspace root with dedup set (#5, added recursive flag to StartFileWatch payload); poll mtime compare > -> != to catch git checkout restoring older mtime (#2); self-save ignore now content-based via active_disk_content_matches_memory so genuine external edits within the 2s window still reload (#3); reduced safety-net poll 1s -> 3s (#6); removed debug eprintln noise (#7).

error_message: Terminal regex highlight (log level / strings / numbers / timestamps) is lost on soft-wrapped lines: every time a long log line wraps to the next visual row, the wrapped portion loses its color.
root_cause: apply_regex_highlights ran the regexes per physical grid row (cols-wide), independently. When a logical log line wraps across rows, the continuation row has no log-level prefix (so it lost the base line color) and a token split across the wrap boundary (e.g. a quoted string "solo_quest...t_backend") doesn't match on the second row because its opening quote is on the first row. The grid never recorded which rows were soft-wrap continuations.
fix: Added wrap_continued flag to TerminalCell, set on the first cell of a row when print_char_at_cursor auto-wraps (cursor_col >= cols, no newline). Rewrote apply_regex_highlights to walk the buffer one LOGICAL line at a time (maximal run of rows where each after the first has wrap_continued), join their text, run regexes on the joined text, and map char index i back to physical (row start + i/cols, col i%cols). Two-phase (collect (row,col,color) under immutable borrow, then apply) to avoid borrow conflicts. Data-type matches pushed lowest-precedence-first so later writes win, preserving original string>number>bool>null>time>base-color precedence. Removed set_visible_row_style_fg; added row_is_wrap_continued + set_style_fg_absolute. Tests: apply_regex_highlights_string_spanning_soft_wrap_keeps_color_on_continuation, apply_regex_highlights_log_level_spans_soft_wrap.

error_message: Accepting a multi-line ghost text fills with wrong indent / extra tabs and cursor looks like it's not at the end; single-line is fine
root_cause: sanitize_inline_suggestion only stripped an echoed line-prefix when its trim_start() was non-empty. On a fresh indented line the line_prefix is whitespace-only (e.g. 8 spaces or tabs), so the guard skipped stripping. Codestral re-emits that leading whitespace (verified: caret after 8 spaces -> output starts with 8 spaces), so accept inserted it AFTER the caret's existing indentation = double indent on line 1. Single-line completions don't hit this because the caret usually sits mid-expression (non-whitespace prefix). The buffer/cursor math itself is correct (proven by new accept_multiline_preserves_text_and_cursor_at_end test); the 'cursor not at end' perception was the double-indent shifting the caret right of where the ghost preview ended.
fix: Rewrote the prefix-strip in sanitize_inline_suggestion: if line_prefix is non-empty, FIRST try strip_prefix(full line_prefix) (covers whitespace-only echo), else fall back to the trim_start() remainder. Deeper-than-caret indentation is preserved (only the echoed caret-level whitespace is removed). Added tests strips_echoed_indentation_on_fresh_line, keeps_deeper_indentation_relative_to_caret, and accept_multiline_preserves_text_and_cursor_at_end. Known minor: during streaming the ghost-text PREVIEW shows the un-sanitized chunks (echoed indent) until the final result re-sanitizes; accept always uses the sanitized value.

error_message: User: type code, move caret elsewhere, THEN the AI ghost text appears at the new spot and follows the cursor; changes during debounce were not cancelled
file: src/app/event_loop/setup.rs, src/app/event_loop/application.rs, src/app/event_loop/commands_editor.rs, src/app/event_loop/commands_lsp.rs, src/app/event_loop/async_results/ai.rs, src/app/event_loop/mod.rs
root_cause: Only insert-typing commands cancelled/re-queued the inline pipeline. Cursor motion, mouse clicks, Escape, and buffer switches never cancelled the pending debounce or the in-flight request and never bumped ai_inline_revision, so a late result passed the bridge revision gate. The ghost text is stored as bare text with no position anchor and renders at the live caret, so the stale suggestion appeared at — and followed — whatever position the caret had moved to. flush_pending_ai_inline_completion also captured prefix/suffix at flush time, not queue time.
fix: Added ai_inline_anchor: Option<(Option<PathBuf>, usize)> on AppShell anchoring the whole pipeline (pending -> in-flight -> visible ghost) to (buffer, caret, Insert mode). queue_ai_inline_completion sets it; enforce_ai_inline_anchor() runs every about_to_wait pass before the flush and on mismatch drops the pending request, cancels the in-flight token, bumps ai_inline_revision (bridge drops late results as stale), and clears visible ghost text. flush re-validates the anchor before submitting. handle_ai_result (chunk + result arms) drops payloads when the anchor is no longer current. Legitimate caret moves keep the ghost by re-anchoring: prefix-retained typing (commands_editor.rs) and partial word accept AiAcceptInlineWord (commands_lsp.rs).

fix: Added current_right_terminal_bounds() mirroring the render-path term_bounds (sidebar minus RIGHT_DOCK_OUTLINE_INSET and RIGHT_TAB_STRIP_HEIGHT). right_terminal_mouse_cell_at / right_terminal_mouse_targeted / handle_right_terminal_mouse_input now use it, so the strip band is excluded and clicks there fall through to the tab handler.

error_message: Mouse wheel doesn't scroll the right-dock agent terminal for Claude/Codex (worked for opencode)
root_cause: right_terminal_mouse_cell_at computed the SGR wheel cell from the full sidebar bounds, but the grid is rendered at term_bounds (offset down by inset + strip_h ~52px). Forwarded wheel coordinates were shifted up by several rows; opencode tolerated it, stricter TUIs ignored wheel events landing outside their scroll pane.
fix: Same current_right_terminal_bounds() correction so wheel cell coordinates map to the actually-rendered grid region. NOTE: the ANSI parser still ignores private modes (ESC[?...h/l -> AnsiEvent::Unknown at ansi_parser.rs:424), so there is no alt-screen/mouse-mode tracking; if a TUI never enables mouse reporting, wheel forwarding still won't scroll it (would need mode tracking + arrow-key fallback).

error_message: Killing agent (Ctrl-C) in right dock doesn't return to provider picker and leaves garbled leftover text
root_cause: spawn_right_agent_terminal (picker launch) ran the agent INSIDE a login shell via startup command '{command}\r'. Killing/quitting the agent dropped back to a live shell prompt instead of closing the PTY, so PtySessionClosed never fired -> grid not cleared, right_pty_session_id stayed Some -> picker never re-shown. (ensure_right_opencode_terminal already avoided this by spawning directly.)
fix: Startup command is now 'exec {command}\r' so the login shell is replaced by the agent (keeps login PATH resolution). When the agent exits/killed the PTY closes -> PtySessionClosed clears the grid and sets right_pty_session_id=None -> the AI Chat picker auto-renders again.

error_message: Right-dock tab strip has no rounded (slice) top corners like the bottom dock terminal tab title
root_cause: build_right_tab_strip drew the strip background and active-tab fills as plain square rects flush to the panel edge, so the panel's rounded focus-ring outline met square strip corners.
fix: Strip background now drawn with .with_radius(panel_corner_radius); the active first/last tab rounds its outer corner to match while interior active tabs stay square (mirrors the bottom dock rounded-panel look).

error_message: After agent (claude/codex) exits via Ctrl-C, the dead TUI text stays on screen behind the re-shown agent picker (UI not cleared)
root_cause: PtySessionClosed handler for the right PTY set app.last_right_terminal_bounds = None BEFORE the redraw. The render-time cleanup that drops the renderer's uploaded terminal glyphs only runs in the `else if self.last_right_terminal_bounds.is_some()` branch — which was now skipped — so clear_right_terminal() never fired and the old glyphs lingered. (The grid model was reset, but the GPU surface was not.)
fix: Call renderer.clear_right_terminal() directly inside the PtySessionClosed handler right after nulling the bounds, guaranteeing the surface is blanked the moment the PTY closes (bug-156's exec change is what makes the PTY actually close).

error_message: Right-dock tab strip rounding wrong: should round ONLY top-left (first tab) and top-right (last tab); active top accent bar overflows outside the panel outline
root_cause: RegionDrawInstance/region.wgsl only supported a single uniform border_radius, so the earlier with_radius fix rounded all four corners (and every active tab), creating notches; and the active accent bar spanned the full tab width flush to the panel edge, overrunning the rounded focus-ring corner.
fix: Added per-corner radius: RegionInstanceRaw now carries corner_radii:[f32;4] (same 48-byte footprint, replacing border_radius+_pad), vertex attr Float32->Float32x4, and region.wgsl picks the radius per quadrant ([TL,TR,BR,BL]). with_radius still sets all four (identical SDF when equal -> existing UI unaffected); new with_corner_radii for partial rounding. build_right_tab_strip now rounds only the strip's two top corners (radius = panel_corner_radius - RIGHT_DOCK_OUTLINE_INSET), rounds only the outer corner of the first/last active tab, and insets the accent bar by the radius on the outer side so it no longer overflows. Added a naga parse+validate test (region_shader_is_valid_wgsl) since the shader only compiles at GPU init.

error_message: Cmd-R (and other Cmd shortcuts) lost behavior while focused on the AI Chat agent terminal / picker / test runner — should work regardless of tab
root_cause: The per-focus interceptors run before keymap resolution: focus==AiChat returned route_ai_chat_input (which swallows non-nav keys), and TerminalFocus forwarded everything except a tiny allow-list to the PTY as raw bytes. So cmd+r (bound globally to app.focus_inspector) never reached input_map.resolve when an agent terminal/picker/test-runner had focus.
fix: Added a global-Cmd resolver at the top of route() (after the zen-leader check, before the focus interceptors): if normalized.has_command_modifier() and input_map.resolve(...) yields a binding, dispatch it. Cmd combos never go to a PTY, and context-scoped bindings still win since resolve is given the current context; unbound Cmd keys fall through to normal routing.

error_message: Quick-resize (space r r) only worked while the main editor was focused, and the keymap felt broken — could not resize the explorer/terminal in place
file: src/app/input_map/mod.rs, src/app/event_loop/commands_settings_helpers.rs, src/app/event_loop/commands_settings.rs, config/keymaps/default.toml, src/app/resolved_keymap.rs, src/core/commands.rs, src/core/command_ids.rs, src/core/command_dispatch/mod.rs, src/render/renderer/ui/statusbar.rs
root_cause: Two issues. (1) Reachability: command_allowed_in_context() hard-gated EnterResize to InputFocusContext::Editor, so `<leader>r r` did nothing when the explorer/terminal held focus; once in resize mode FocusTarget was therefore always CenterEditor. (2) Once in resize mode under a non-editor focus, the single-key resolver branched on focus BEFORE any mode check, so resize keys would have been swallowed by resolve_explorer_focus/terminal handlers. The old h/H/l/L commands were also gated to CenterEditor in their helpers.
fix: Relaxed command_allowed_in_context() to allow EnterResize from Editor/Explorer/Terminal; added `<leader>r r` bindings under the explorer and terminal_normal keymap modes (TOML + resolved_keymap built-in); added an EditorMode::Resize precedence branch at the top of InputMap::resolve so resize-mode keys own h/j/k/l + Esc regardless of focus. Replaced the 8 width/edge commands with 6 focus-aware ones: h/l/j/k resize the focused panel (sidebar width, bottom height) or push the editor's docks when the editor is focused; H/L grow the left/right dock. New focus-aware helpers resize_focused_width/height + resize_left_dock/right_dock backed by a single clamped adjust_dock(ResizeDock). Added a RESIZE-mode key hint line in the status bar.

error_message: Selecting 'Fetch LeetCode Problem' from the command palette did nothing — the problem-input prompt never appeared
root_cause: handle_palette_and_open_command had keep-open carve-outs for LeetCodeLanguageSelector/PythonEnvSelector/DartEnvSelector but NOT LeetCodeProblemInput. The command-list path dispatches FilePickerConfirmSelection -> ExecuteCommand(FetchLeetCodeProblem) which opens LeetCodeProblemInput, then fell through to release_focus_mode_to_editor() which exited PaletteFocus and tore the overlay down. The existing test passed because it dispatched Command::FetchLeetCodeProblem directly, bypassing the confirm flow.

error_message: Cannot paste (Cmd+V) into the LeetCode problem-input command palette (id/slug/URL prompt)
root_cause: The EditorPaste handler routes clipboard text into the palette query only for an explicit allow-list of CommandPaletteModes; LeetCodeProblemInput (and LeetCodeLanguageSelector) were missing, so paste fell through to insert_text_at_cursor on the editor buffer instead.
fix: Added CommandPaletteMode::LeetCodeProblemInput and LeetCodeLanguageSelector to the paste allow-list at editing.rs. Regression test editor_paste_appends_to_leetcode_problem_input_query.

error_message: Buffer-tab result lists such as Fuzzy Finder/Live Grep and References allow selection to move into bottom results, but the list viewport does not scroll down and the selected row is hidden by overflow.
root_cause: The result window estimated capacity from content height divided only by row height. File/group headers also consume vertical space, so the computed start index could render fewer items than estimated and stop before the selected item.
fix: Added a shared grouped-list window calculation that simulates row plus group-header height and advances the start until the selected item fits. Applied it to Live Grep, References, and Diagnostics, with a regression test covering a selected final item across multiple groups.

error_message: LeetCode AI test-case generation produced cases identical to existing ones (first 2 always verbatim copies of cached cases), plus invalid edge cases (empty/single-element arrays) and ~40% arithmetically wrong expected outputs.
root_cause: Two causes. (1) Duplication: build_stratified_prompt fed the first 2 cached cases as 'Existing examples' and instructed '2 like the examples', so at temp 0.1 the model echoed them back verbatim; the degenerate edge-case guidance ('empty/zero, single element') also violated problem constraints. (2) Wrong expected values: mistral/codestral-2508 is a non-reasoning code model that cannot reliably compute expected outputs (measured ~40% wrong, systematic index patterns like [1,3]/[0,2] regardless of arithmetic); the verify pass was also OFF by default (leetcode_verify_enabled unwrap_or(false)) so nothing caught the errors.
fix: Rewrote build_stratified_prompt to list ALL existing cases as 'must NOT repeat', require 5 NEW/DIFFERENT, constraint-valid, small inputs, and re-check expected before emitting. Flipped leetcode_verify_enabled default to true (second re-trace pass). Switched leetcode.provider.model from codestral-2508 to mistral/mistral-large-latest, which benchmarked 0/5 wrong across repeated runs at ~2.7s (codestral was ~40% wrong). Verified: 844 lib tests pass; live generate 0 dupes/0 wrong, verify pass corrects injected errors.

error_message: Yank flash remains visible on screen until another key is pressed, and is too opaque (completely covers text).
root_cause: (1) The winit event loop went to sleep (ControlFlow::Wait) between keypresses, meaning tick_yank_flash was never called to check for timer expiration. (2) tick_yank_flash returned false when the timer expired, preventing request_redraw. (3) Opacity used self.theme.ui.accent directly (alpha = 1.0), obscuring the text.
fix: (1) Added a getter for yank_flash_start in AppState, and factored this into winit's next_deadline calculation in about_to_wait to wake the loop up at the next frame (every 8ms) while yank flash is active. (2) Reduced duration to 50ms as preferred. (3) Reduced yank flash alpha by multiplying by 0.25.

error_message: Yank flash still remains visible until another keypress after the first wakeup/50ms fix, and the highlight is still too opaque.
root_cause: The timer woke the event loop and requested redraws, but tick-only redraws did not mark the editor overlay layer dirty. add_yank_flash_overlay appends into editor_overlay_chrome_instances only when update_editor_overlays runs, so cached chrome could remain onscreen until a later key/movement invalidated editor_caret_needs_layout.
fix: tick_yank_flash now marks editor_caret_needs_layout when flash is active or expiring, forcing the overlay layer to rebuild and clear without any keypress. The flash lifecycle uses a shared 50ms duration constant, clearing bumps revision, and max overlay alpha was lowered to 0.14.

error_message: Vim % match-bracket command was missing, and the editor had no live matched-bracket highlight or jump-target ripple feedback.

Covered with app-state, dispatch, input-map, and event-loop tests.

error_message: User reported the editor breadcrumb / tab-bar was not visible at all in the main editor.
